elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: § 15.1 says "MSL agrees to protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM" — an express defence duty, but it runs only to IBM; no IBM affiliates are named and the redline does not add them.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Indemnity covers "any and all claims, damages, liabilities, losses and expenses" but the beneficiary is "IBM" alone; affiliates are omitted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: § 15.1(a) covers "infringement by MSL in rendering performance under this Agreement ... or by any MSL procured Parts, processes, designs, deliverables ... of any patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work right or trade secret".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Only § 15.1(a) and the two carve-out sentences are supplied; any further subsections of § 15.1 (e.g. breach of law) are not in the rendered text, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No unauthorised-access/disclosure trigger appears in the supplied § 15.1 text; the drafter expressly declined to add one.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No gross negligence/wilful misconduct trigger appears in the rendered paragraphs; the rationale confirms it was not sought.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts a notice/control/cooperation procedure exists in § 15, but no such operative wording is in the cited or rendered paragraphs, so it cannot be verified here.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No control-of-defence language appears in the supplied text of § 15.1–15.3.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation covenant appears in the supplied text.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rationale states the only IBM indemnity sits in § 14 of a Loan Agreement limited to Loaned Items, but that clause is not rendered, so its scope (which is not content/breach-of-law limited on its face) cannot be verified.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: § 15.1 chapeau plus (a): MSL must "protect, defend, hold harmless, and indemnify IBM" for third-party infringement of "any patent, trademark, trade name, copyright, mask work right or trade secret valid anywhere in the world".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification-based exclusion exists (the quoted trademark carve-out is about IBM-selected marks, not modifications). The absence is more Customer-favourable, so the condition does not apply and the element is satisfied; the mapping's quote is mismatched but harmless.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination exclusion is present (the quoted IBM-design-defect carve-out is a specification exclusion). Absence favours Customer, so no repair needed.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall have no obligation to indemnify IBM ... to the extent that such third party claim (i) is caused by MSL's material compliance with a written specification provided by an authorized representative of IBM or (ii) results from a defective design ... the result of the written specifications or designs provided by ... IBM."

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Redlined § 15.2(b): "MSL shall, at its own expense, in order to remedy any such infringement for the future, procure any necessary license rights, or make use of non-infringing designs, processes, Parts, deliverables or other materials" — the discretionary "may, at its sole discretion" is removed.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: Added: "and if none of the foregoing is available, MSL shall refund to IBM the fees paid for the affected Products."

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Redlined § 15.3(b): "Except for MSL's indemnification obligations under Section 15.1, which are limited to three times (3X) the annual fees paid to MSL under this Agreement, the total liability ... is limited to three percent (3%) of the value of the bill of materials ..." — the indemnity is carved out of the 3% cap and given the 3X super-cap.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: a genuine MSL IP defence-and-indemnity already exists, the Customer-caused exclusions are present (and the two permissive exclusions that are absent are Customer-favourable), and the two operations convert the cure remedy from discretionary to mandatory, add a refund backstop, and carve the indemnity out of the 3% bill-of-materials cap at the 3X annual-fees super-cap.

Preferred level is not reached: affiliates are not added as beneficiaries of the defence/indemnity, and the data-breach, breach-of-law and gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers plus the notice/control/cooperation procedure and the narrowing of any Customer indemnity are not in the rendered operative text. This is correctly handled as short-of-preferred commentary rather than additional edits.

Minimality holds: the only deletions are "may, at its sole discretion and" (necessary to make the cure mandatory) and nothing outside the two target elements; "at its own expense" is retained existing language, the general 3% cap survives for all other liability, and no survival tail, procedure or extra damages category was imported.

Intent is preserved: the cap carve-out is drafted as an exception rather than a rewrite, so the parties' general liability allocation, timing and bill-of-materials measure remain intact, and the IBM-caused exclusions in § 15.1 continue to qualify the enlarged remedy.

Drafting improvement (not a failure): "annual fees paid to MSL under this Agreement" and "the fees paid for the affected Products" use "fees" in an agreement whose consideration is Product purchase prices measured by bill-of-materials value. Consider "amounts paid or payable to MSL under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim" and "the amounts paid for the affected Products" to avoid an argument that no "fees" exist.

Housekeeping: the element mapping's quotes for the modifications and combinations exclusions cite the trademark and IBM-design carve-outs, which do not evidence those exclusions; the elements are nevertheless satisfied because they are permissive and their absence benefits IBM.

Note for the negotiation record: the carve-out lifts the cap for all of § 15.1 (not just subsection (a)), which is Customer-favourable relative to the current 3% ceiling; confirm no other § 15.1 head of indemnity was previously uncapped.
